beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Om Mali. This video is about the price panel, turning S E C filings into an actual per share price history for private A I companies, and catching the one thing that would have silently ruined it. The arithmetic is one line. Everything hard is in deciding which rows deserve to be in it.

show.event: Cream Claude composer, empty. Serif greeting 'Ahoj, HAI' + terracotta spark above it.
The ask types itself into the composer, character by character.
Send button arms terracotta; running indicator reads 'pricing 5,806 holdings…'.
Three output lines land in sequence — the ask arrives ANSWERED (COLD OPEN LAW).

props.segment: Building the Marks Panel and the Split Detector
props.command: Build the per-share price panel: value divided by share count, once per security per fund per quarter. Then catch the stock splits before they enter the series as crashes — and do not let the detector decide what a step actually is.
output: 5,479 marks from 5,806 filed holdings — reconciles exactly
split detector: window was ±0.02, the test case is 11.9300 — missed
now a relative 1% rule; 3 suspected splits, all decided by a person

beats.narration_text: Here is the whole week. Value divided by share count, once per security per fund per quarter, gives five thousand four hundred and seventy-nine marks. That part is one line of arithmetic. The part that took the week is a detector for stock splits, because a split makes a price look like a crash. It found three. It could not tell me what any of them were.

shot.visual_intent: The BLUF and the division of labour: the panel is one line, the detector is the week, and the detector does not decide.

show.event: The formula sets in serif at display size.

show.at: on 'five thousand four hundred and seventy-nine marks'
show.event: The mark count resolves beneath it.
Two halves land — the arithmetic, and the week.

show.at: on 'could not tell me what any of them were'
show.event: A 'decide' chip lands and is struck through.

props.sparkLine: One line of arithmetic. A week of judgment.
props.headline: Value ÷ shares.
props.formulaNote: once per security, per fund, per quarter — 5,479 marks

halves.sub: 3 companies threw a suspected split — the ratio classifies none of them

props.rule: A split makes a price look like a crash. Catching the step is arithmetic; deciding what it is took a person and a written reason on all 7 quarantined series.

beats.narration_text: Five thousand eight hundred and six filed holdings go in. Twenty-eight were rejected last month as belonging to nothing. Seventy-two sit on filings a later amendment replaced. The remaining five thousand seven hundred and six aggregate into marks. It reconciles exactly, and nothing gets dropped for being awkward.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w7-panel.png. The subtraction happens on screen, so 'reconciles' is shown rather than asserted.

show.at: on 'five thousand eight hundred and six'
show.event: The starting count resolves at display size.
28 and 72 are subtracted in sequence, each with its reason.
5,706 lines collapse into 5,479 marks.
The arithmetic lands across the foot as a single line.

props.sparkLine: Every filed row accounts for itself.
props.title: Where every filed row went
props.subtitle: one mark = one fund's recorded price for one security at one period end

deductions.label: rejected last month — belonged to nothing

blocks.label: blended lines: the price belongs to neither class

props.blocksLabel: held out of the change series
props.reconcileNote: 5,806 − 28 − 72 = 5,706. Reconciles exactly. Nothing dropped for being awkward.

beats.narration_text: Here is why the detector matters. Perplexity went from six hundred and ninety-five dollars a share to fifty-eight. Read naively that is a ninety-two percent collapse, and it would have entered the price history as one. It is not a collapse. It is a stock split, and a price series has to know the difference.

shot.visual_intent: The drop must be FELT before it is explained — the beat exists so the viewer understands why a detector is worth a week.

show.event: The before price sets at display size.
A line falls off a cliff to the after price.
The naive reading lands in terracotta beneath the drop.
The naive reading is struck and the real cause replaces it.

props.title: A split looks exactly like a crash
props.note: The same shape, either way. A change series that cannot tell them apart publishes a 92% crash that never happened.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata_week7.json — quarantine, COM:UNSPECIFIED; the −92% is derived from the two prices

beats.narration_text: My detector used a window of plus or minus nought point nought two around whole numbers. Perplexity's ratio is eleven point nine three, nought point nought seven away from twelve. The window misses it by a factor of three. It looked correct only because the other Perplexity step landed on exactly ten. The rule is now a relative one percent window, imported by the detector and the review queue.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w7-tolerance.png. The mark must sit visibly OUTSIDE the old box — the miss is a distance, so it is measured on screen.

show.at: on 'plus or minus nought point nought two'
show.event: A number line draws with a narrow grey box around 12.
A terracotta mark lands OUTSIDE the box, and the gap is measured.
The gap and the window are shown against each other.
The decoy ratio appears at exactly 10, inside its own window.
The wider new window draws and contains the 11.93 mark.

props.sparkLine: Too narrow to catch its own test case.
props.title: The window that missed its own test case
props.decoyLabel: the other Perplexity step — it lands on a whole number, inside any window, which is why an absolute rule passed its own smoke test
props.fix: Now a RELATIVE 1% window. One rule, imported by the detector and the review queue.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata_week7.json — tolerance = 0.01, quarantine ratios. the previous window (±0.02) is from narration_script.md / plan.md — figdata_week7.json carries only the rule that ships.

beats.narration_text: But catching a step is not deciding what it is. Three companies threw one, and the ratio cannot tell you which is which. The share count can. Perplexity's preferred line went from nineteen thousand shares to a hundred and ninety-three thousand, while the dollar value did not move by a cent. Ten times the shares, exactly the same money.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w7-evidence.png, first row. This is the T. Rowe PREFERRED line at ratio 10.0000 — a different security from the 11.93 common line, and labelled as such.

show.event: The security and class are named so this row cannot be confused with the 11.93 one.
Three filed rows land: shares, value, implied price.
The share count column lights terracotta on the ×10 step.

show.at: on 'did not move by a cent'
show.event: The two identical filed values are bracketed, shown to the cent.

props.title: The ratio cannot tell you. The share count can.
props.security: PERPLEXITY AI SER E-1 CVT PFD PP
props.verdict: Ten times the shares. Exactly the same money. That is a split.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata_week7.json — perplexity, the LARGEST position (the figure used to pick the smallest; the run log cites the largest). Values to the cent, un-rounded.

beats.narration_text: Anthropic held the same eighty-nine thousand shares in all thirteen quarters. Only the value moved, and the step reverses the next quarter, which a split never does. SpaceX the same: share count constant, value exactly doubled. Splits move the share count. Repricings move the value. A person made all three calls, and wrote the reason down.

shot.visual_intent: The rule first, then each case tested against it. The two NOT-a-split verdicts come first so the beat is not a victory lap for the detector.

show.event: The two-line rule sets at display size: splits move the share count, repricings move the value.

show.at: on 'Anthropic held the same eighty-nine thousand'
show.event: The Anthropic case lands with its constant share count and its reversal.
The SpaceX case lands — constant shares, value exactly doubled.

show.at: on 'a person made all three calls'
show.event: The reviewer's name lands against all three verdicts.

cases.evidence: $12.18 → $48.94 → $30.00 — it reverses. A split never does.
value unchanged at $13,488,132.50 — the shares moved, not the money

props.countNote: All 7 quarantined series carry a written reason and a human name. 3 were splits, 4 were not.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata_week7.json — quarantine notes, anthropic and spacex series

beats.narration_text: One of those is subtler. Eleven point nine three is not a split factor. It is a ten for one split and a sixteen percent markdown that landed in the same quarter. Divide by eleven point nine three and you erase a real price move. Divide by ten and it survives. So the panel records what a person decided to divide by, separately from what the machine measured.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w7-factor.png. Red marks the CORRECT answer, never the wrong one — DESIGN.md forbids red as a warning colour (README correction 3).

show.at: on 'eleven point nine three is not a split factor'
show.event: The measured ratio sets alone.

show.at: on 'a ten for one split and a sixteen percent markdown'
show.event: It decomposes into two parts; only the split half takes the accent.

show.at: on 'divide by eleven point nine three'
show.event: The wrong outcome lands — the markdown erased.

show.at: on 'divide by ten and it survives'
show.event: The right outcome lands beside it and keeps the accent.

props.title: 11.93 is not a split factor

parts.label: and a markdown in the same quarter

props.rule: So the panel stores both: ratio 11.9300 as measured, factor 10.0000 as decided. Week 8 divides by the decided one.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata_week7.json — quarantine COM:UNSPECIFIED: ratio_min/max and factor are separate fields

beats.narration_text: The plan listed seven checks for this panel. Six pass. The seventh needs filings the S E C has not published yet, and it reports that rather than quietly passing. And one of the six expected four managers to agree on Anthropic's price. Ten do, in two clusters four thousandths of a dollar apart.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w7-checks.png. The counts are computed from the table (README correction 4 — the title used to hardcode '0 fail' and disagreed with its own rows).

show.event: Seven rows land, six ticking in sequence.
The seventh lands hollow, with its reason beside it.
The expected 4 is replaced by the measured 10.
The two price clusters and their manager lists land beneath.

props.sparkLine: Six pass. One says why it cannot.

props.subtitle: counted from the table, never hardcoded

Anthropic 5/29-5/31 pair at ~589

beats.narration_text: Week seven on one page. Five thousand four hundred and seventy-nine marks, value divided by share count, every filed holding accounted for. A detector whose window was too narrow to catch its own test case, now a relative one percent rule. Three companies threw a suspected split and the ratio could not tell them apart. Share counts could, and a person made every call with the reason written down. Six of seven checks pass, and the seventh says why it cannot. Next week: how often these marks actually move.

show.event: The Claude artifact page opens — Building the Marks Panel and the Split Detector, week 7.
Five findings stagger in, one per spoken clause.

props.artifactTitle: Building the Marks Panel and the Split Detector — week 7
artifactLines: 5,479 marks — value ÷ share count, per security per fund per period. 5,806 − 28 rejected − 72 superseded = 5,706. Reconciles exactly.
The split detector's window was ±0.02 absolute and missed its own test case at 11.9300 by a factor of 3. It is now a relative 1% rule, imported by both the detector and the review queue.
3 companies threw a suspected split; the ratio cannot classify them. Share counts can: ×10 shares at an unchanged $13,488,132.50 is a split, constant shares with a reversing step is not.
Ratio is not factor. 11.9300 = a 10-for-1 split AND a 16% markdown in one quarter. The panel stores measured and decided separately; 7 marks stay blocked until Week 8 divides.
6 of 7 checks pass, 0 fail, 1 unreachable and says so. One expected 4 managers to agree on Anthropic's price; 10 do.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Take a threshold in your own code. An absolute tolerance, a cut off, a magic number. Find the case it was written for, then check whether it would still catch that case today. Mine would not, and it looked fine because a second case happened to land inside it. A threshold that has never been tested against the thing it exists to catch is just a guess with a number on it.

show.event: Composer returns, greeting reads 'Your turn.'
The suggested prompt types itself in as the narration reads it aloud, verbatim.
Running text reads 'paste this into Claude…' while the narration discusses what to look for.

props.segment: Building the Marks Panel and the Split Detector
props.command: Find every absolute threshold in my code — tolerances, cut-offs, magic numbers. For each one, tell me which case it was written to catch, then test it against that case as the data looks today. Where an absolute window should be a relative one, say so, and tell me which other module would have to import the same rule.
